svg.title: Figure 6-2. Safety mechanisms by element (WP-S-03 §6)
svg.desc: 45 safety mechanisms of WP-S-03 §6 grouped by element. E-03a: SM-01 Torque magnitude limit (speed-dependent) (partly), SM-02 Torque rate and RT-window limit (implemented), SM-03 Measured-torque tracking (implemented), SM-04 Authority gating (PCM edge, brake, gas, steer request) (partly), SM-05 Driver-torque override monitor (not implemented), SM-06 EPS status monitor (partly), SM-07 Longitudinal bounds and jerk limits (partly), SM-08 Active safe-state frame (not implemented), SM-09 RX timeout (implemented), SM-10 RX checksum + length (partly), SM-11 RX rate, frozen-content and cross-checks (partly), SM-13 Command-frame freshness (partly), SM-24 Relay malfunction detection (traffic-based) (implemented), SM-29 Engagement follows PCM cruise; revoke on SoC "not engaged" (partly), SM-35 Forwarding with fixed block list and forwarding supervision (partly), SM-36 PCS and DSU message TX gate (implemented), SM-39 Per-ID TX rate supervision (implemented). E-03b: SM-12 Heartbeat + control-loop liveness (partly), SM-14 SPI CRC + sequence counter + bounds checks (partly), SM-16 Fault → safe state (not implemented), SM-22 Configuration lock and command gating (partly), SM-23 SoC-independent siren (partly), SM-38 Post-load TX read-back (not implemented). E-04a: SM-15 Independent watchdog (implemented), SM-17 RAM ECC, flash CRC, register checks (partly), SM-18 Clock monitor (CSS + cross-check) (partly), SM-19 Supply monitor (BOR, PVD, input voltage) (unknown), SM-20 Relay readback and latch (partly), SM-21 MPU isolation (not implemented), SM-40 Car-side transceiver supervision (partly), SM-41 MCU die-temperature monitor (partly), SM-42 Harness orientation and connection detection (partly). E-01: SM-25 Host fault classification and freshness (partly), SM-26 Driver monitoring (partly), SM-27 Excessive-actuation detector (implemented), SM-28 Controller margin (partly), SM-30 Engagement and authority mismatch detection (SoC side) (partly), SM-31 HMI path liveness and audible minimum (partly), SM-32 Announced, bounded item-initiated deceleration (partly), SM-33 FCW input freshness and false-alarm rate (partly), SM-34 PCM ACC-fault reaction (implemented), SM-37 Stock AEB/FCW event indication (implemented), SM-43 ACC cancel on every fault-induced disengagement (implemented), SM-44 Start-up fault-code entry check (implemented), SM-45 Stock-AEB stand-down (implemented).

Status is the latest in §6 (the reference build where it is given). Nothing is verified: implemented means the code does it, drawn blue, not green. Mixed statuses (Impl / Partial) count as partly.
DC targets are targets for the FMEDA (WP-H-03) and software safety analysis (WP-W-04), not demonstrated. Generated by fig_s03_mechanisms.py from WP-S-03 §3.1 and §6.

g.text: Terms: ABS anti-lock braking system; on the Toyota, the ABS/VSC ECU that also runs stability control · ACC adaptive cruise control · AEB automatic emergency braking · AOU-nn assumption of use (WP-C-01 §7); an R

suffix marks the FSC's refined version · ASIL Automotive Safety Integrity Level, A (lowest) to D (highest), from ISO 26262 · BOR brown-out reset (MCU supply monitor) · CAN controller area network: the vehicle's data

bus · CRC cyclic redundancy check · CSS clock security system (MCU clock monitor) · DC diagnostic coverage: the share of faults a safety mechanism detects · DM driver monitoring · DSU driving support unit (Toyota's

radar cruise module) · E-nn element of the item (WP-C-01 §3.1), E-01…E-06 · ECC error-correcting code (memory) · EPS electric power steering · FCW forward collision warning · FDCAN CAN with flexible data rate (the

MCU's CAN controller) · FMEDA failure modes, effects and diagnostic analysis (hardware metrics) · HMI human-machine interface: display, sounds, cluster · LKA lane keeping assist · MCU microcontroller: the panda

safety processor (STM32H7) · ML machine learning · MPU memory protection unit · PCM powertrain control module (engine and drive) · PCS pre-collision system: Toyota's stock collision warning and braking · PVD

programmable voltage detector (MCU supply monitor) · QM quality managed: no ASIL; ordinary quality processes suffice · RAM random-access memory · RT real time · RX receive · SM-nn safety mechanism (TSC §6) · SoC

system on chip: the comma device's main processor, running openpilot (QM) · SOTIF safety of the intended functionality (ISO 21448): hazards with nothing failing · SPI serial peripheral interface (the link between

SoC and MCU) · TSR-nn technical safety requirement (WP-S-02) · TX transmit · VSC vehicle stability control (Toyota's stability system) · WP-nn work product, e.g. WP-C-04; the letter is its area (M management, C
concept, S system, H hardware, W software, V validation, P processes, A analyses, O operation, K safety case)
